title: Starlight · Signal — eight bars from Return, looping #Shorts
description:
A seamless loop. Let it repeat — it is cut to an exact whole number of the chord cycle, so it never lands on a join.

Five minutes of the tightened shimmer, with a hole cut in the middle of it. Eight bars where the pulse simply stops and the same notes go back to being a wash — then it returns at double speed for a twenty-four-bar climb — at this tempo, the longest unbroken rise in any of these. It ends as a wash again.

THE PULSED ORIGINAL, TWICE OVER — the pulse stops dead in the middle · D minor · 66 BPM · ⚠ this one has a pulse

This is an original piece, not a cover. It was written after a reference track — А. Рыбников, «Свет звёзд», from the 1981 film «Через тернии к звёздам» — and what it borrows is an approach, not any of his material: sustained strings, a wordless voice on top, harmony that barely moves, and all of the motion in tone colour rather than in rhythm. There are no drums and no bass ostinato anywhere in it.

This one loops. It is an exact 8-bar cut — 1 complete turn of the 8-bar chord cycle in this music — so the chord that follows the last bar is the chord the first bar starts on — it can repeat indefinitely without a seam. The reverb tail is carried across the join rather than cut off. 29 seconds; the full five-minute version is on the channel.

The picture is a constant-Q spectrogram: the octave rulers run left to right from C1 to C7, so a note sits at the same place across the frame every time it is played, which a normal spectrogram does not give you. Stereo waveform below, playhead and progress across the bottom.

DAW Pro is a macOS digital audio workstation built so an AI agent can drive it as well as a person can — every instrument, effect and mix move here was made inside it.
